content: 1. DHEA and herbal supplements may increase the levels or effects of quinine by influencing the metabolism of the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor and currently unknown. Close monitoring is advised. 2. Digoxin can increase the levels or effects of quinine due to competition for renal tubular clearance of basic (cationic) drugs. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 3. Diltiazem may increase the levels or effects of quinine by affecting the metabolism of the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 4. Both disopyramide and quinine can prolong the QTc interval. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 5. Dofetilide increases the levels or effects of quinine through competition for renal tubular clearance of basic (cationic) drugs. Additionally, both dofetilide and quinine can prolong the QTc interval. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 6. Dolasetron and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 7. Donepezil and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. This combination is considered serious, and alternative drugs should be used. 8. Doxepin and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. This combination is considered serious, and alternative drugs should be used. 9. Dronedarone increases the levels or effects of quinine by affecting the metabolism of the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Although quinine levels are not significantly increased, the combination is contraindicated due to the potential for both drugs to prolong the QTc interval. 10. Droperidol and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 11. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of quinine by influencing the metabolism of the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor and currently unknown. Close monitoring is advised. 12. Dulaglutide may impact the absorption of oral medications by slowing gastric emptying. This is particularly important for drugs with a narrow therapeutic index. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 13. Dupilumab may normalize the formation of CYP450 enzymes by reducing cytokine levels during chronic inflammation. When initiating or discontinuing dupilumab in patients taking concomitant CYP450 substrates, especially those with a narrow therapeutic index, therapeutic effects should be closely monitored. 14. Quinine increases the levels or effects of duvelisib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Duvelisib increases the levels or effects of quinine by affecting the metabolism of the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 15. Quinine increases the levels or effects of edoxaban by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. This combination is considered serious, and alternative drugs should be used. Dose adjustments may be required with strong P-gp inhibitors. 16. Efavirenz and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. This combination is considered serious, and alternative drugs should be used. Efavirenz may also decrease the levels or effects of quinine by affecting the metabolism of the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor and currently unknown. 17. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of quinine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Elagolix decreases the levels of quinine by affecting the metabolism of the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 18. Quinine increases the levels of eliglustat by affecting the metabolism of the hepatic enzyme CYP2D6. This combination is contraindicated. Eliglustat also increases the levels of quinine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 19. Encrafenib both inhibits and induces CYP3A4 at clinically relevant plasma concentrations. Encrafenib and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. This combination is considered serious, and alternative drugs should be used. 20. Quinine increases the effects of enoxaparin by an unknown mechanism. This combination is considered serious, and alternative drugs should be used. 21. Quinine and entrectinib both prolong the QTc interval. This combination is considered serious, and alternative drugs should be used. 22. Epcoritamab may suppress CYP enzyme activity by releasing cytokines, leading to increased exposure to CYP substrates. For certain CYP substrates, even minimal changes in concentration can result in serious adverse reactions. Therapy modification should be considered as clinically indicated. 23. Erdafitinib increases the levels or effects of quinine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Quinine increases the levels or effects of erdafitinib by affecting the metabolism of the hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10. This combination is considered serious, and alternative drugs should be used. 24. Eribulin and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. This combination is considered serious, and alternative drugs should be used. If concurrent use is necessary, ECG monitoring is recommended. 25. Erythromycin (base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, and stearate forms) increases the levels or effects of quinine by affecting the metabolism of the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 26. Escitalopram and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 27. Eslicarbazepine acetate decreases the levels or effects of quinine by affecting the metabolism of the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor and currently unknown. 28. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of quinine by affecting the metabolism of the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor and currently unknown. 29. Ezogabine and quinine both increase the risk of QTc interval prolongation. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. QT interval monitoring is particularly important when ezogabine is prescribed with agents known to prolong the QT interval. 30. Fedratinib increases the levels or effects of quinine by affecting the metabolism of the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 31. Ferric maltol may decrease the bioavailability of quinine or other oral drugs. For oral drugs where reduced bioavailability may cause clinically significant effects, separate administration of ferric maltol from these drugs is recommended. 32. Fexinidazole and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. This combination is considered serious, and alternative drugs should be used. Fexinidazole inhibits CYP3A4, which may increase the risk of adverse effects of CYP3A4 substrates. 33. Quinine increases the levels or effects of finerenone by affecting the metabolism of the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 34. Fingolimod and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. This combination is considered serious, and alternative drugs should be used. 35. Flecainide and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 36. Flibanserin increases the levels of quinine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Quinine increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by affecting the metabolism of the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 37. Floxuridine and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 38. Fluconazole increases the levels or effects of quinine by affecting the metabolism of the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor and currently unknown. 39. Fludrocortisone decreases the levels or effects of quinine by affecting the metabolism of the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor and currently unknown. 40. Fluoxetine and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 41. Fluphenazine and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 42. Quinine increases the effects of fondaparinux by an unknown mechanism. This combination is considered serious, and alternative drugs should be used. 43. Formoterol and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 44. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of quinine by affecting the metabolism of the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor and currently unknown. 45. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of quinine by affecting the metabolism of the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor and currently unknown. 46. Foscarnet and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 47. Fosphenytoin decreases the levels or effects of quinine by affecting the metabolism of the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor and currently unknown. 48. Quinine and fostemsavir both prolong the QTc interval. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 49. Gadobenate and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. This combination is considered serious, and alternative drugs should be used. 50. Gemifloxacin and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 51. Gepirone and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 52. Gilteritinib and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. This combination is considered serious, and alternative drugs should be used. 53. Quinine and givinostat both prolong the QTc interval. This combination is considered serious, and alternative drugs should be used. If coadministration is unavoidable, ECG monitoring is recommended. 54. Quinine and glasdegib both prolong the QTc interval. This combination is considered serious, and alternative drugs should be used. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor for increased risk of QTc interval prolongation. 55. Quinine increases the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases the levels or effects of quinine by the same mechanism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 56. Glofitamab may suppress CYP enzyme activity by releasing cytokines, leading to increased exposure to CYP substrates. Therapy modification should be considered as clinically indicated.
